title: Smart session shingling batcher with KV-delta tiling for streaming chat
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a new batch formation heuristic (Smart Session Shingling) that groups streaming chat requests by 'shingle' similarity and KV-delta tiling to improve GPU memory packing and reduce prefix duplication while preserving tail latency SLOs.
background: Current session-aware batchers either aggressively merge sessions (reducing throughput variance but increasing KV duplication) or strictly separate sessions (preserving KV locality but underutilizing GPU slabs). We observed pathological cases where long-running chats with small updates thrash the KV cache and force early slab spills, increasing p50/p95 token cost. Existing tickets (see dependencies) target related improvements but do not address the combination of temporal locality (small deltas) and partial prefix reuse in streaming chat flows.
proposed_solution: Introduce a two-stage heuristic: 1) Session Shingling: compute lightweight content fingerprints over the last N tokens (a sliding 'shingle' window) and use a locality-aware hash to group requests that are likely to share KV entries; 2) KV-Delta Tiling: when forming a batch, explicitly detect requests that only append small deltas to a shared prefix and place them into a compact tile that shares KV slots and avoids replicated KV cache entries. The batcher will maintain a per-GPU tiling table with soft quotas and a dynamic eviction scoring that factors in shingle similarity, delta size, session age, and estimated remaining length. Additionally, implement a low-water gating mechanism that prioritizes latency-critical sessions and uses preemptive micro-shearing to split oversized candidate tiles when they threaten to exceed GPU slab budgets. The runtime exposes knobs for tile_max_tokens, shingle_window, similarity_threshold, and low_water_margin.
tasks: Spec: write detailed design doc with diagrams for shingle hashing and tiling layout
Prototype shingle fingerprint (fast rolling hash) in runtime mock harness
Implement tiling table and integration with existing batch allocator
Add estimator for delta size and prefix share ratio to predict KV duplication
GPU memory safety checks and slab-reserve hooks for tiling allocations
Unit + integration tests for correctness of shared-KV execution path
Benchmark microbench: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory usage, token cost
Dashboard and SLO alerts: add charts for tile_hit_rate, kv_duplication_factor, slab_spill_events
Rollout: feature flag, gradual canary, fallback to existing batcher on degradation
acceptance_criteria: No regression in p50 latency for streaming chat (<= 5ms change at p50 on canary workload)
p95 latency degradation <= 5% versus baseline in steady-state accepted traffic
Reduce measured KV duplication factor by >= 20% on mixed conversational workloads
Reduce GPU slab spill events by >= 30% on long-running conversation workload
Token generation cost improvement >= 8% for targeted workloads (measured with same model and sequence length distributions)
Operational visibility: graphs for tile_hit_rate, avg_delta_size, kv_duplication_factor available in console
Graceful fallback: if tiling table exceed thresholds or memory failsafety triggers, batcher falls back to stable allocator without request loss
testing_plan: Synthetic replay tests: curated traces with small append deltas, long prefix reuse, and high churn sessions
A/B microbench on dedicated cluster: 24h runs measuring cost and latency under identical load
Stress test: simultaneous burst of 5k streaming sessions to validate slab-reserve and preemptive micro-shearing
Chaos test: force GC/eviction events and ensure fallback path preserves correctness
End-to-end correctness: iterate token outputs against baseline for a set of deterministic prompts to avoid functional regressions
rollout_plan: Internal canary: enable on internal dataset with 10% of traffic for 48h
Customer pilot: opt-in tenant(s) with telemetry monitoring for one week
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% if key metrics (p95, slab_spill, kv_duplication) within thresholds
Automatic rollback: if p95 increases > 8% or slab_spill > baseline + 25% for 30min, rollback to previous allocator
